title: Demo Snack
scenes[8].sceneName: Repeat and acknowledge Child A again
scenes[0].speech[0].speechText: They took all the oranges! That’s not fair!
scenes[3].speech[0].speechText: They took all the oranges and it’s not fair! They can’t have them all.
scenes[6].speech[0].speechText: I want to hold the oranges now.
scenes[7].speech[0].speechText: You eat bananas. I get oranges.
scenes[8].speech[0].speechText: All the crackers are gone already, so we have to give oranges to Elders first. Auntie Priscilla is visiting.
scenes[1].hint: This is part of C-ontrol - Use Sportscasting and neutrally but assertively describe what you observe so the children know you are there to support them both. E.g. “I see you are both upset about something”.
scenes[2].hint: This is part of L-isten Fully. Find out what happened from both children’s perspectives. E.g. “Both of you tell us what happened. Pass me the oranges to keep safe while we talk it through”
scenes[3].hint: This is part of L-isten Fully. Acknowledge feelings and perspective by reflecting the emotion and re-stating the child’s point of view. E.g. “You’re upset that she is holding all the oranges”.
scenes[4].hint: This is part of L-isten Fully. Acknowledge feelings and perspective by reflecting the emotion and re-stating the child’s point of view. E.g. “You are feeling worried because all the crackers are gone”.
scenes[5].hint: This is part of E-xplore solutions. Tell both children they need to brainstorm solutions to come up with one and that they will all have to agree on the solution. E.g. “What are some ideas to solve the problem?  We will find one that is ok for everyone”.
scenes[6].hint: This is part of E-xplore solutions. Paraphrase each child’s idea and ask the other child if they agree. E.g. Say “She wants to hold all the oranges. Is that ok with you?”
scenes[7].hint: This is part of E-xplore solutions. Paraphrase each child’s idea and ask the other child if they agree. E.g. Say “You’re not ok with that. You suggest that we switch bananas and oranges. Is that ok with you?”.
scenes[8].hint: This is part of E-xplore solutions. Paraphrase each child’s idea and ask the other child if they agree. E.g. Say: “You think we should save the oranges to share with the elders. Is that ok with you?”.
scenes[9].hint: This is part of R – Resume, Encourage, & Expectations. Use Encouragement and describe the children’s efforts and State Clear Expectations about what they children can do to implement the solution. E.g. Say: “You solved the problem together!  Put the oranges on the table and go and let’s go and get the Elders”.
